issues.element: Token trend: solid, dashed and dotted violet lines overlap at nearly every peak and trough. The dash differences are clear in the key but considerably harder to follow inside the narrow plot.
issues.fix: Strengthen the visual hierarchy within the violet family: give the total line a heavier solid stroke, increase the difference between long-dash and round-dot patterns, and reduce the fill opacity. Keep the legend swatches identical to their plotted strokes.

issues.element: Token trend: narrow plotting area carries three independent scales, but only the total-token axis remains beside the lines; the other scale ranges live in the legend.
issues.fix: Keep the separate-scale explanation immediately next to the legend and make it explicit that the left axis is only Total tokens. Preserve the range labels and data-table alternative; test the stronger stroke treatments at this exact width.

issues.element: Initial viewport shows only the top of Usage trend after two rows of tall sparkline cards.
issues.fix: Use a short-window card variant that keeps a suitably sized sparkline beside its value where the card has room, and reduces unused vertical card space without shrinking the plot labels.

issues.element: Initial viewport reaches the Token trend heading and axis labels, with virtually none of the data visible. Token cards remain tall even where three columns provide room beside each number.
issues.fix: Base sparkline placement on the individual card width/count, and retain only the essential overlapping-counter warning before the chart with the detailed caveat available through a compact disclosure.

issues.element: Notice ends with the fragment “Legacy cache-write lifetime unavailable.”
issues.fix: Use a complete, specific sentence such as “Legacy records do not report the cache-write retention period.” Keep the surrounding explanation that missing components are excluded.

issues.element: The pre-chart notice combines execution duration, speed calculation, request-detail location, TTFT comparability and missing aggregate statistics into one dense paragraph.
issues.fix: Keep the timing definition and mixed-method TTFT warning visible in two short sentences, and place the remaining measurement details in an explicitly labelled disclosure. Preserve every limitation; do not imply that TTFT is comparable.

issues.element: Two very wide, tall plots are stacked, so comparing duration with TTFT requires a long vertical scan despite ample width.
issues.fix: At an ultrawide breakpoint, place the two trend panels side by side with equal plot heights, aligned time axes, and their own labelled millisecond scales.

issues.element: Three KPI cards and three breakdown values repeat “Unavailable”; a long generic measurement paragraph separates them from two repeated “No measured values” panels. The page never states the overall condition clearly.
issues.fix: Add one concise state explanation that events are present but timing measurements are unavailable for this interval. Reuse the existing no-measurement condition; do not invent a cause. Keep the charts’ time context, drilldown and data-table access.

issues.element: The request table stretches a small amount of row content across almost the whole ultrawide display, separating model, outcome and numbers by large gaps.
issues.fix: Constrain the table’s reading width or explicitly allocate narrower numeric/action columns while leaving the model column flexible. Keep row tracking easy without spreading every column evenly.

issues.element: The reference notice, Model Rates heading, source warning and units note occupy most of the space before the first rate row.
issues.fix: Consolidate the repeated current-configured-rates context into the units caption, keep the source warning prominent, and shorten the reference notice while preserving that rates are current rather than historical.

issues.element: Model identifiers are regular-weight in Requests but bold in Model Rates; row details use an outlined button in Requests and a bare disclosure in Model Rates.
issues.fix: Use the same identifier emphasis in both tables and align the visual weight and placement of row-level details controls while preserving their respective interactions.
